name: MI-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Thanedar lost renomination
McKinney's strong fundraising and outside support
model.rationale: The D+22 district fundamentals make a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely, and markets price the race at roughly 98% Democratic. McKinney's solid fundraising and outside backing reinforce the baseline, with only a modest trim for the open-seat uncertainty.
model.watch: A late scandal or unusually strong Republican spending could narrow the margin, though a GOP win remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Shri Thanedar (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Detroit-area MI-13 is a heavily Democratic district with a D+22 partisan lean, and the incumbent Shri Thanedar will not appear on the ballot after losing renomination. Donavan McKinney, who defeated him in the primary, enters the general with about $1.4 million raised and roughly $930,000 in outside support, far outpacing any visible spending against him. Republican T. P. Nykoriak has no reported fundraising, and minor-party and independent candidates lack resources.

Prediction markets price the Democratic hold near 98%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic win in the mid-twenties.
